hints: Focus on what that wavenumber window means, which specific double bond gives a strong peak between 1610 and 1750 cm-1?
Work out what P must be from CH4O with no rings, can an alcohol or ether contain that double bond?
Check Q and R for a C=O group, a carboxylic acid and an aldehyde both contain it, so decide which combination fits.
walkthrough:
**Recall what absorbs at 1610-1750 cm-1**

Think of this as the carbonyl fingerprint region. A strong, sharp peak here means a $\text{C=O}$ double bond is present.

Rule to remember:
$$1610-1750 \text{ cm}^{-1} \text{ = strong } \text{C=O} \text{ stretch}$$

**Deduce the structure of P**

P is $\text{CH}_4\text{O}$ and is not cyclic. With only one carbon and four hydrogens, it must be methanol, $\text{CH}_3\text{OH}$.

It contains only $\text{C-H}$, $\text{O-H}$ and $\text{C-O}$ single bonds, so no $\text{C=O}$ and no peak in that region.

**Deduce the structures of Q and R**

Q is $\text{CH}_2\text{O}_2$ and is not cyclic. To fit two O atoms on one carbon, it must be methanoic acid, $\text{HCOOH}$.

R is $\text{CH}_2\text{O}$ and is not cyclic. To fit one O on one carbon with two H atoms, it must be methanal, $\text{HCHO}$.

Both contain a $\text{C=O}$ group:
$$\text{H-C(=O)-OH (acid) and H-C(=O)-H (aldehyde)}$$

**Conclude which molecules absorb**

Only molecules with $\text{C=O}$ show the strong absorption. That is Q and R only, while P does not.

options.A: Incorrect. Q ($\text{HCOOH}$) does absorb because its carboxylic acid $\text{C=O}$ gives a strong peak, but this misses R. R ($\text{HCHO}$) also has a $\text{C=O}$ and so also absorbs.
options.B: Incorrect. R ($\text{HCHO}$) does absorb because its aldehyde $\text{C=O}$ gives a strong peak, but this misses Q. Q ($\text{HCOOH}$) also has a $\text{C=O}$ and so also absorbs.
options.C: Correct. Q is methanoic acid with a $\text{C=O}$ in $\text{COOH}$, and R is methanal with a $\text{C=O}$ in $\text{CHO}$. Both give a strong carbonyl stretch at 1610-1750 cm-1, while P ($\text{CH}_3\text{OH}$) has no $\text{C=O}$.
options.D: Incorrect. This wrongly includes P. P is $\text{CH}_4\text{O}$ ($\text{CH}_3\text{OH}$), an alcohol with only single bonds. With no $\text{C=O}$ group it shows no strong absorption in the 1610-1750 cm-1 region.
